_meta.language: Thai (spoken, casual street register) + English gloss

address_terms.เฮีย: older brother (Sino-Thai) — customers call the cook this; the shop is named after it
address_terms.เจ๊: older sister (Sino-Thai) — female shopkeepers / auntie vendors
address_terms.พี่: older sibling, polite default for strangers older than you
address_terms.น้อง: younger sibling — vendors call young customers / staff this
address_terms.หลวงพี่ / หลวงพ่อ: how laypeople address a monk (young / old); monks call themselves อาตมา
address_terms.ครับ / ค่ะ / คะ / จ้ะ / จ้า: polite particles: ครับ (male), ค่ะ statement / คะ question (female), จ้ะ/จ้า friendly

_meta.guardrails: No royals, politicians, real celebrities or brands. Monks/temples respectful. Ghost folklore OK.
